- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep decline, reduce subsequent forecast values by 5–15% to correct for overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently lags behind forecast by 2–3 days, apply a 1–2 day lag correction by shifting forecast down 1–2% per day.  
- If forecast mean is consistently higher than true mean over 3–5 days, apply a 2–5% downward adjustment to the 30-day average.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and forecast deviates > 3% from recent 7-day average, revert to 7-day moving average for 3–5 days.
